title: Certify full package lifecycle: upgrade, rollback, cross-desktop switch, and removal
summary: A certification test script (packaging/tests/test_lifecycle_cert.sh) stages split packages via stage.sh --package core|gnome|kde into a DESTDIR fake-root and exercises the full lifecycle: fresh install, upgrade (re-stage over existing), add desktop, cross-desktop switch, rollback (remove desktop packages), full removal (uninstall.sh), and password-login preservation. Byte/hash (sha256) receipts prove runtime state (templates, templates.key, models, backoff.json) is preserved through upgrade and desktop add/remove, then fully purged on removal. Stock files (/usr/bin/ls, /etc/pam.d/system-auth) survive the purge with sha256 receipt match. Zero /etc/pam.d modifications at every stage (PAM default-off). Since clean distros cannot be run in CI, real distro upgrade/rollback on a live VM (pacman -U, dnf upgrade, apt upgrade) is documented as WITHHELD. The structural lifecycle validation is the CI-testable portion and passes 82/82 assertions.
method: DESTDIR fake-root staging via stage.sh --package core|gnome|kde, simulating each lifecycle phase. (a) Fresh install: stage core, verify all 21 core manifest files + 13 dirs present, no /etc/pam.d. (b) Upgrade: seed runtime state (fake template, key, backoff, model) with sha256 receipts, re-stage core over existing, verify sha256 receipts match (preservation), manifest re-copied, no stale files in namtor-owned dirs. (c) Add desktop: stage gnome over core, verify 4 gnome files added, core intact, template preserved. (d) Cross-desktop: stage kde over core+gnome, verify 3 kde files added, gnome files coexist (split packages coexist), core intact. (e) Rollback: remove all gnome+kde manifest files, verify core fully present, template preserved. (f) Full removal: run uninstall.sh with DESTDIR, verify zero manifest files remain, namtor-specific dirs purged, generated_state purged, stock files survive (sha256 receipt match). (g) Password login preservation: verify 0 pam_namtor references under /etc/pam.d at every lifecycle stage (fresh, upgrade, gnome add, kde add, removal), lifecycle.sh post-install does not call pam-edit.

staging.note: stage.sh is idempotent (re-staging overwrites files deterministically). Runtime state under /var/lib/namtor/ (generated_state) is not touched by stage.sh — preserved across re-staging.

purge_receipts.stock_ls: sha256 before == sha256 after (uninstall only removes namtor paths)
purge_receipts.stock_pam: sha256 before == sha256 after (uninstall never touches stock PAM files)

checks: 0 pam_namtor refs after fresh core install
lifecycle.sh post-install does not call pam-edit (structural check)
g_password_login_preservation.rationale: PAM is default-off at install time. No /etc/pam.d modifications happen during stage.sh or uninstall.sh. PAM services are enabled only via the D-Bus Manager2 interface (polkit-authorized, transactional). Password login (pam_unix / pam_systemd_home) is never disrupted.

real_pacman_upgrade.reason: Requires a clean Arch VM with the package installed via pacman -U, then upgrading to a new version. CI uses DESTDIR fake-root staging, which cannot run pacman.

real_dnf_upgrade.reason: Requires a clean Fedora VM with the package installed via dnf, then upgrading. CI uses DESTDIR fake-root staging.

real_apt_upgrade.reason: Requires a clean Debian VM with the package installed via apt, then upgrading. CI uses DESTDIR fake-root staging.

real_package_rollback.reason: Requires a clean distro VM with a previous package version installed, then downgrading (pacman -U old.pkg, dnf downgrade, apt install old). CI simulates rollback by removing desktop manifest files from the staged root.

real_cross_desktop_live_session.reason: Requires a live desktop session with both GNOME and KDE installed, switching between them. CI verifies file-level coexistence structurally.

real_removal_with_systemd.reason: Requires a clean distro VM with systemd running to verify systemctl disable, userdel, groupdel during removal. CI runs uninstall.sh with DESTDIR (skips systemd/userdel).

files_not_modified: No Rust source, Cargo.toml, or distro packaging modified
